item.title: Can Indian citizens apply for H-1B renewal from the UAE? Here’s what Reddit post read
item.description: Indian H-1B visa holders can now renew their visas from third countries like the UAE, provided they have valid residency permits. One applicant successfully renewed their H-1B in Dubai after facing significant delays in India, highlighting a viable alternative for navigating appointment backlogs.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘You’ll be the next Kirk’: Minnesota fraud exposé YouTuber Nick Shirley says he’s facing death threats
item.description: Youtuber Nick Shirley faces death threats after exposing Minnesota's childcare fraud, with accusers warning he'll be "kirked." He expressed concern for his family, especially his younger sister, who is receiving media calls.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Can the US revoke citizenship? Trump administration weighs denaturalisation in Minnesota fraud case
item.description: The Trump administration explored denaturalizing Somali-Americans in Minnesota involved in fraud, aiming to revoke citizenship for those who illegally obtained tax dollars. This move followed charges against 86 individuals, predominantly Somali-Americans, for exploiting federal funds intended for hungry children. Officials stated denaturalization is a tool at their disposal to address such fraud.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Watch: Sleeping driver stopped on Will Rogers Turnpike — How a trooper stopped vehicle before a crash on an Oklahoma turnpike
item.description: A trooper on the Will Rogers Turnpike in Oklahoma successfully stopped a vehicle driven by a nearly 20-hour working driver who had fallen asleep. The driver's Kia, with lane assist engaged, was traveling slowly and weaving within its lane. The driver was issued a citation, and the Highway Patrol emphasized the severe dangers of drowsy driving.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Who is Cabot Phillips? Candace Owens challenges claims after viral posts connect him to Charlie Kirk controversy
item.description: A viral murder theory on X tried to link Cabot Phillips to claims about Charlie Kirk, but no crime occurred. Candace Owens questioned timelines and media clips, while Phillips denied all claims and shared personal details to explain his location. Charlie Kirk is alive, and no official source supports the theory.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: ‘Rot in hell’: Trump unleashes fury on Jared Polis, Dan Rubinstein over Tina Peters’ imprisonment
item.description: Former President Trump launched a scathing attack on Colorado Governor Jared Polis and DA Dan Rubinstein, calling for them to "rot in hell" over the imprisonment of ex-clerk Tina Peters. Peters, convicted for tampering with voting machines, received a nine-year sentence. Trump's clemency attempt was rejected, highlighting a clash over state versus federal authority.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Queen Camilla breaks silence: Shares assault ordeal to highlight violence; urges open dialogue
item.description: Queen Camilla has bravely shared her personal experience of an indecent assault from her teenage years, highlighting its connection to the ongoing epidemic of violence against women. Speaking out, she aims to use her royal platform to address this critical issue, emphasizing the importance of breaking the taboo surrounding domestic abuse and encouraging others to share their stories.

item.title: Zohran Mamdani to use Quran at swearing-in: First NYC Mayor to do so; will feature 3 unique Qurans
item.description: Zohran Mamdani makes history as the first NYC mayor to swear on the Quran, representing diverse demographics. He will use multiple Qurans, including his grandfather's and one from the New York Public Library belonging to Arturo Schomburg. This symbolic act highlights faith, identity, and New York's rich history, correcting a long-standing absence of Muslim representation in public life.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Explained: Who is Alaa Abd el-Fattah, and why is his return to the UK making headlines
item.description: Alaa Abd el-Fattah, once a symbol of Arab Spring idealism, now faces controversy in the UK after his release from Egyptian prison. His return ignited debate over old social media posts and the vetting process for his British citizenship. This episode highlights the complex challenges liberal democracies face when balancing humanitarian advocacy with national security.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Indonesia raises alert for the Mount Bur Ni Telong volcano following a spike of activity
item.description: Mount Bur Ni Telong in Indonesia's Aceh province is on high alert, raised to its second highest level due to increased volcanic earthquakes and activity. Authorities are urging residents to stay clear of the crater and gas zones, especially during bad weather. This heightened alert comes as the region is still recovering from devastating floods and landslides.

item.title: ‘A new era’: Zohran Mamdani appoints al Qaeda detainee’s lawyer Ramzi Kassem as NYC chief counsel - who is he?
item.description: New York Mayor-elect Zohran Mamdani has appointed lawyer Ramzi Kassem as the city's chief counsel. Kassem, who previously represented an individual in an al-Qaeda-related terrorism case and advised the Biden administration on immigration policy, will bring his extensive legal experience to the role. He also co-founded a project focused on law enforcement accountability and has represented students detained by ICE.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Zohran Mamdani to assume office: NYC to get new mayor; attorney general Letitia James to administer midnight oath
item.description: Zohran Mamdani will be sworn in as New York City's new mayor on New Year's Day with two ceremonies. The first, a private family oath at the historic City Hall subway station, will be administered by Attorney General Letitia James. A public celebration with a second oath on the steps of City Hall, led by Senator Bernie Sanders, will follow.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Macron backs bill: France plans social media ban for under-15s; draft law cites screen time risks
item.description: France is preparing a legislative push to curb excessive screen time, proposing a ban on social media for children under 15 by next September. The draft law, backed by President Macron, also includes a ban on mobile phones in secondary schools. This initiative follows similar moves by Australia and aims to protect minors from inappropriate content and cyber-harassment.

item.title: Asia rings in 2026 with Sydney remembering its worst mass shooting
Explained: How the Israel issue is splintering MAGA
item.description: Once a bedrock of Republican consensus, support for Israel is fracturing within the MAGA movement. This ideological split, fueled by generational, theological, and ideological differences, exposes fault lines and a disturbing rise in antisemitic rhetoric. The future of the right hinges on how this conflict over Israel is resolved.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Body found near San Antonio home of missing Texas teen Camila Mendoza Olmos
item.description: A body was discovered near the San Antonio home of missing teen Camila Mendoza Olmos. The discovery occurred during a renewed search effort. Authorities are working to formally identify the body and determine the cause of death. A firearm was found near the location. Camila was last seen on Christmas Eve. Investigations are ongoing.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Will Saudi Arabia succeed in turning its vast desert landscape green by planting 10 billion trees?
item.description: Saudi Arabia is attempting one of the most ambitious environmental transformations ever undertaken in an arid country. Through the Saudi Green Initiative, the Kingdom is planting billions of trees, restoring degraded land, expanding protected areas and rebuilding water systems, grounding its climate goals in science, long-term planning and economic diversification as it prepares for a future beyond oil.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Mizkif claims OTK lost relevance after his exit as old tensions resurface following ExtraEmily’s announcement
item.description: Mizkif claimed One True King lost relevance immediately after his departure, reacting to news that ExtraEmily’s OTK contract is ending. He also explained why Jschlatt left the group, saying the creator disliked the spotlight and streaming. Mizkif’s comments have reignited debate about OTK’s direction and its future without key founding members.
